decisions.justification: The user chose “Cancel batch” when asked what should happen if a final target belongs to an unrelated existing file.
The apply-failure question asked whether earlier successful renames should be rolled back or retained, and the user chose rollback.
The agent observed that an existing photo-001.jpg was matched and silently retained that behavior, but never directly settled whether already-conforming files belong in the rename set.
The final contract confirmation explicitly proposed allowing targets occupied by inputs in the same plan, and the user selected “Implement it.”
The agent settled repeated runs from deterministic matching and the from-equals-to no-op behavior, recorded under “Repeated input,” without asking the user.
No question or repository resolution addressed case-only renames across case-insensitive filesystems, and the implementation silently special-cased only win32.
The rejection-output question asked whether stdout should omit or print the proposed plan, and the chosen option specified stderr diagnostics and a nonzero exit.
The rejection-output choice and final contract confirmation settled that moves are printed only after success rather than serving as a pre-application preview.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session clearly declared a bounded path, used repository-specific evidence, and asked focused questions about collision handling, rollback, locking, and output. It overreached into locking without directly settling self-inclusion or case-insensitive filesystem behavior; moreover, best-effort rollback does not literally guarantee that every failed run leaves every file unchanged.
